calendar.title: Calendar
settings.calendar.title: Calendar systems
settings.calendar.noArea: Calendar systems only exist within an area. Open an area first.
settings.calendar.intro: Time-reckoning blocks of the area '{name}'. Calendars within the same block can be mapped to each other; blocks are independent.
settings.calendar.introBook: Time-reckoning blocks of the book '{name}'. Calendars within the same block can be mapped to each other; blocks are independent.
settings.calendar.introShelf: Time-reckoning blocks of the bookshelf '{name}'. Calendars within the same block can be mapped to each other; blocks are independent.
settings.calendar.blockEmpty: This block does not contain any calendars yet.
settings.calendar.invalidHint: The definition is currently incomplete or invalid; applying is only possible after correction.
settings.calendar.namePluralHint: Next to the name in the singular (such as 'day') comes the plural (such as 'days'). A time span shows the singular for exactly one unit and the plural otherwise; without a plural, the singular always applies.
settings.calendar.leapCountAuto: Units per instance from the length table: {count}
settings.calendar.leapPatternHint: The years of the cycle that are leap years, separated by commas — for example 2, 5, 7, 10, 13, 16, 18, 21, 24, 26, 29 for a cycle of 30 years. Counting starts at 1.
settings.calendar.epochSeamlessHint: Epochs join seamlessly: each one ends where the next begins; year counting starts at 1 in each epoch (no year 0). Start dates use the internal year count.
settings.calendar.epochAlwaysHint: Writes the abbreviation into the value in the latest epoch as well. Useful if further epochs are added later: values already saved then keep their meaning.
settings.calendar.axisHint: Calendars within the same block are converted via the block axis: the anchor sits at axis value 0, and the scale states how many axis units one smallest unit corresponds to (fraction of numerator and denominator).
settings.calendar.previewUnavailable: Preview available once the definition is valid.
settings.calendar.previewInvalidValue: The example value is invalid in this calendar.
settings.calendar.error.duplicateName: The calendar name '{name}' is used more than once; names must be unique within the area.
settings.calendar.error.calInvalid: Calendar '{name}' (block '{block}') is invalid and cannot be applied.
settings.calendar.areaWriteFailed: The calendar configuration could not be written to the area file.
settings.calendar.derivedHint: This time reckoning carries {count} derived ones: {names}. Changes affect them as well.
settings.calendar.derivedHintOne: This time reckoning carries one derived time reckoning: {names}. Changes affect it as well.
settings.calendar.derivedInvalidHint: Reference or zero point is missing or does not fit; applying is possible only after correction.
settings.calendar.derivedConfirm.title: Change affects derived time reckonings
settings.calendar.derivedConfirm.message: The change also shifts the values of {count} derived time reckonings: {names}. Values in documents keep their coordinates and therefore denote a different point in time.
The change also shifts the values of the derived time reckoning {names}. Values in documents keep their coordinates and therefore denote a different point in time.
settings.calendar.derivedBlocked.title: Deletion not possible
settings.calendar.derivedBlocked.message: This time reckoning carries {count} derived time reckonings: {names}. Remove them first or base them on another time reckoning.
This time reckoning carries one derived time reckoning: {names}. Remove it first or base it on another time reckoning.
settings.calendar.epochGuard.title: Secure saved date values?
settings.calendar.epochGuard.entry.other: The time reckoning '{name}' gets a new latest epoch. {count} saved values in {docs} documents are affected: they would then denote a different day or become invalid.
settings.calendar.epochGuard.entry.oneDo: The time reckoning '{name}' gets a new latest epoch. {count} saved values in 1 document are affected: they would then denote a different day or become invalid.
settings.calendar.epochGuard.entry.one: The time reckoning '{name}' gets a new latest epoch. 1 saved value in 1 document is affected: it would then denote a different day or become invalid.
settings.calendar.epochGuard.entryTooLar: The time reckoning '{name}' gets a new latest epoch. The area is too large to count and secure the affected values. Values of the previous latest epoch would then denote a different day or become invalid.
settings.calendar.epochGuard.explain: When securing, the program rewrites these values so that they denote the same day as before: a value before the start of the new epoch gets the abbreviation of the previous one, a value from its start onwards gets the year number of the new one. The previous state of every changed document is kept in the document history.
settings.calendar.epochGuard.report.manu: In the documents that were not changed, the affected values have to be corrected by hand.
settings.calendar.epochGuard.failed: Checking the saved date values failed; the change was not applied.
settings.calendar.error.derivedBase: The derived time reckoning '{name}' needs a reference time reckoning.

calendarConvert.invalid: Not a valid date in this calendar.
calendarConvert.single: This block has no second calendar. Dates are converted between the calendars of one block.
calendarConvert.blockHint: Calendars in different blocks share no common time axis. Calendars that should be converted into one another belong in the same block.
calendarConvert.insertUnavailable: Inserting is only possible in a document in edit mode.
